newsitem.title: USA: US rail traffic up from yr ago despite UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: US rail traffic up from yr ago despite UPS strike.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal volume rose in the week ended August 9 compared to the same week in 1996 despite the ongoing United Parcel Service strike, a railroad policy group said Thursday.
The Association of American Railroads reported a total of 350,006 carloads on railroads in the United States last week, up 1.3 percent from 345,368 in the year-ago week.
AAR said intermodal volume, which does not include carloads, stood at 166,146 trailers and containers in the week, up 5.2 percent from 157,914 a year ago.
Ton-miles rose 2.3 percent to 26.8 billion last week from 26.2 billion in the same 1996 week, AAR said. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
"Reductions in UPS movements were partially offset by the resulting increases in shipments by the U.S. Post Office," AAR Senior Assistant Vice President Craig Rockey, said in a statement.

"While having the potential for greater impact on rail traffic in the coming weeks, as of the week ending August 9, the UPS strike appears to have had limited influence on intermodal traffic volumes," Rockey added.

AAR said the biggest increases in carloads from a year ago included grain, which rose 23.1 percent in the week to 21,306 carloads from 17,311, and grain mill products, which climbed 10.8 percent to 10,027 carloads from 9,051 last year.

Loadings of lumber and wood products stood at 5,702 carloads last week, up 8.1 percent from 5,275 a year ago, while motor vehicles and equipment rose 6.8 percent to 20,059 carloads from 18,780, AAR said.
But farm products other than grain plunged 24 percent in the August 9 week to 887 carloads from 1,167 a year ago, AAR said, while metallic ores fell 10.9 percent to 19,886 carloads from 22,321.
Coke carloads were down 9.7 percent to 4,779 in the week from 5,292 a year ago, while nonmetallic minerals loadings stood at 9,223, down 8.9 percent from 10,122 last year.

In the first 32 weeks of 1997, AAR said carload volume rose 1.3 percent to 10.86 million from 10.72 in the same 1996 period, while intermodal volume increased 8.3 percent to 5.25 million trailers and containers from 4.84 million.

Separately, AAR reported that U.S. carloads on the two Canada-based railroads totalled 50,448 in the August 9 week, up 10.9 percent from the year-ago week, and 22,835 trailers and containers, up 10 percent from a year ago.

Combined U.S. carload volume in the United States and Canada-based railroads for the first 32 weeks of 1997 totaled 12.54 million, up 1.6 percent from the same 1996 period, and 6.02 million trailers and containers, up 8.7 percent from the year-ago period, AAR said.
